anomalies.observed: On the MCU sheet, the TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1 (U2) IN pin 1 is connected to the +12V rail (with C13 0.1 uF from that node to GND), while only DIAG_EN pin 2 is connected to NET0003, which is the ESP32-C3-MINI-1 (U8) GPIO1 pin 13 net.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that the heater high-side switch's IN and DIAG_EN pins (1/2) are both driven from ESP32 GPIO1, i.e. the HEATER/NET0003 control net, not tied to +12V.

evidence.quote: MCU sheet: U2 TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1, pin 1 IN connected to +12V and C13 0.1uF to GND; pin 2 DIAG_EN connected to NET0003; U8 ESP32-C3-MINI-1 pin 13 GPIO1 has label NET0003.
IN/DIAG_EN (pins 1/2) are both driven from ESP32 GPIO1 (net /Microcontroller/HEATER)

anomalies.impact: The heater output would be enabled whenever the 12 V supply is present, independent of firmware GPIO1 control. The bang-bang heater control loop could not turn the heater off, creating an overheating hazard.

parsed.summary: The schematic shows a functional deviation on the heater high-side switch: its IN pin is tied to +12V instead of the ESP32 heater-control GPIO net, so the heater would be permanently enabled rather than firmware-controlled.
